data.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
data.summary: SVG has no capital gains, inheritance, gift or net wealth tax. Ordinarily resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income (top 28%); whether this reaches foreign portfolio dividends is not verified. Residents who are not ordinarily resident are taxed on foreign income only when remitted. Low confidence on dividends.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Ordinarily resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income at 10%/20%/28%; residents who are not ordinarily resident are taxed on foreign income only when received in SVG. No capital gains, inheritance or net wealth tax.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if present 183 days in a calendar year (with continuity rules); ordinarily resident if a permanent home in SVG plus presence in the year.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are not subject to tax.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Transfer tax of 5% each for buyer and seller on immovable property and share transfers; non-residents need an alien landholding licence (4%-10%).

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: St. Vincent and the Grenadines Highlights 2026

capital_gains.rate_basis: Deloitte SVG Highlights 2026: 'Capital gains are not subject to tax.'
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading profits would be business income taxed at up to 28%.

dividends.summary: Dividends are not taxed in the hands of resident individuals: Income Tax Act s. 36(1) excludes 'the actual amount of any dividend accrued' from the assessable income of every resident person, without limiting this to SVG companies. Foreign portfolio dividends are therefore 0%, whether or not remitted. SVG levies no dividend withholding.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: The exclusion applies to all resident persons and does not depend on the dividends being kept abroad (not a remittance-basis result).

open_questions: The IRD's consolidation of Cap. 435 runs to 2009; later amendment acts (2019, 2020, Finance Act 2023) are scanned images and were not read for any change to s. 36.
dividends.rate_basis: Income Tax Act Cap. 435 s. 36(1) (consolidation to 2009, published by the Inland Revenue Department): 'the assessable income of every resident person shall not include the actual amount of any dividend accrued to that person'; s. 77, to which s. 36(1) is subject, was repealed by Act No. 10 of 1998. Deloitte 2026 likewise says dividend income is not taxed. Source-country withholding on US/EU dividends (e.g. 30% US, no US treaty) is a final cost and cannot be credited.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on dividends. 20% on interest/royalties to non-residents.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Individuals: residential property tax at a low rate on market value (Deloitte lists 0.008%).

open_questions: Whether the 5% transfer tax on shares applies to gifts or estate transfers of SVG company shares not verified.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax reported by Deloitte; transfer tax applies to transfers of immovable property and shares.

residency.tax_residency_test: 183 days in a calendar year (with continuity rules); ordinarily resident with a permanent home and presence. Not ordinarily resident: foreign income taxed only when received in SVG.

cost_of_living.notes: Not sourced. Re-checked 15 Oct 2026: no long-term 4-5 bedroom rental with a monthly rent (Kingstown, Villa/Indian Bay, Bequia listings found were nightly or weekly holiday rates) and no private secondary school fee schedule online.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets wherever they live; the app adds the federal layer. There is no local tax here to credit against US tax on portfolio income, so a US family pays the full US rates. No Puerto Rico-style exclusion applies.
open_questions: Cost of living not sourced (re-checked 15 Oct 2026): no agency long-let listing for a 4-5 bedroom house with a monthly rent (Liberty Properties lists only commercial and small residential lets; longtermlettings.com 1 house; The Grenadines Collection and others quote weekly holiday rates) and no private/international secondary school fee schedule online. Both need a direct quote from a local agent and school.

succession.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
succession.summary: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines allows wide testamentary freedom, with no reserved share and no inheritance tax per a commercial guide. Common-law trusts apply. No private foundation law was found and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states the conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
succession.trust_note: Not in the HCCH status table. Wills fall under the Wills Act, Cap. 495 and intestacy under the Intestates Estates Act (commercial guide). No trust statute or foundation law was read.
open_questions: Only a commercial blog was found; the statutes were not read.
Existence of international trust or foundation statutes not confirmed.
Private foundations: no source found either way; not finding a foundation law is not evidence that there is none.
